svg.title: Range restriction in a hiring screen
svg.desc: Two scatter panels. Panel A shows all applicants against job performance, with a vertical screening threshold; the region left of the threshold and above the median hire performance is highlighted as candidates who were screened out but would have performed. Panel B shows only the hired sample, with the x-axis rescaled, and the fitted line visibly flatter than the true relationship. The observed correlation is much lower than the true correlation.
svg.text: Range restriction in a hiring screen
A · THE RELATIONSHIP YOU WOULD NEED TO SEE
every applicant — simulated, because this data cannot be collected
60 of the 260 rejected sit in the teal region — below the threshold,
above the performance of the median person who was hired.
B · THE SAMPLE THE COEFFICIENT IS COMPUTED ON
hires only — x-axis rescaled to the selected range
The truncation is not visible from inside this panel. The cloud fills the frame
and the software returns a number.

Simulated. Selection is set at 38% and the true correlation at 0.50, which is generous. Real funnels are tighter and most screens claim less, so the attenuation shown is a conservative version of the effect.
